analysis:
All three changed files are live, env-gated test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live (DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_GEMMA). They ship in no production binary and change no runtime behavior.

GemmaOpenRouterLiveTests.swift (head 62-83) now reassembles streamed tool-call fragments by wire index. It accumulates id, name and arguments per index, and still asserts a single call, the expected tool name, finish_reason 'tool_calls' and valid JSON arguments. It handles a nil index by falling back to fragments.count. This is test-only parsing and touches no keys, attestation, authorization or coordinator contract.

GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift (head 265) adds an exhaustive-switch case for the new .toolCallDelta event. It records an Issue if a named tool_choice call is ever streamed in fragments, which tightens the test assertion.

Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (patch near 389) adds a .toolCallDelta case that keeps only delta.completed whole calls.

The new .toolCallDelta event case and the OpenAIToolCall delta fields (index, optional id/function) are defined in production sources not supplied here. They belong to the same PR, so streaming tool-call fragment emission may change the provider-to-coordinator wire path (TB-002, T-008). I could not review that path. Production code should confirm that fragments are still encrypted per chunk and that fail-closed behavior is preserved. No threat-model asset (A-001, A-003 and the others) or the T-041 cache posture is affected by these test files. No findings from this batch.
